subject.title: fix(runtime): cancelled workflows no longer continue external commands

question: Should a workflow or input resume capability be permanently consumed once the first resumed step-dispatch boundary is crossed and cancellation occurs, while cancellation during async setup remains retryable?
rationale: The patch implements and tests this distinction, but it defines a user-visible retry and persistence contract rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept the dispatch boundary
options.body: Keep the current behavior: setup-time cancellation preserves a resume capability, while post-dispatch cancellation consumes it to prevent replay of external side effects.

options.title: Choose a different retry contract
options.body: Specify a different point at which cancellation consumes resumed state, then revise the cleanup and regression coverage to match that policy.

recommendation.title: Accept the dispatch boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the current behavior: setup-time cancellation preserves a resume capability, while post-dispatch cancellation consumes it to prevent replay of external side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: They implemented the current boundary and can provide the most direct technical context, although the final policy decision needs an area owner.
